stepTitle: Redesign shared web auth token storage
acceptanceCriteria: Web auth no longer persists access/refresh tokens through JS-readable cookies, or the step is intentionally split into a safe staged migration with the highest-risk leak path removed first. Both web apps still authenticate correctly and verification passes.

findings.summary: Session hint cookie name mismatch between server route and rest of codebase
findings.detail: auth-session-route.ts defines AUTH_HINT_COOKIE = 'sb-auth-present' (line 6), but auth-cookie-names.ts exports AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE = 'miospot-web-auth' and all middleware files check for 'miospot-web-auth'. Both web-consumer and web-merchant wire up this server route at /api/auth/session. When the server POST handler sets cookies, it will write 'sb-auth-present', but middleware will look for 'miospot-web-auth' — meaning server-initiated sessions won't keep users logged in through middleware redirects. The server route should import and use AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE from '../lib/auth-cookie-names' instead of defining its own constant.

findings.summary: Preview route hardcodes 'sb-access-token' instead of using ACCESS_TOKEN_COOKIE constant
findings.detail: This server-side route reads the access token cookie with a hardcoded string 'sb-access-token'. If the cookie name ever changes, this route will silently break. It should import ACCESS_TOKEN_COOKIE from '@miospot/web-runtime/lib/auth-cookie-names'.

findings.summary: Preview route hardcodes 'sb-access-token' instead of using ACCESS_TOKEN_COOKIE constant
findings.detail: Same issue as the lookbook preview route — hardcoded cookie name instead of the shared constant.
